a004.name: a004-physical-pool64-control-build
a004.purpose: Build original physical64 storage with identical fixed32-owner diagnostics for separately executed SHA256 model/cache parity
command:
set -e
cargo check --bin test_physical_pool --bin compare_physical_pool_group --bin compare_physical_pool_history > experiments/physical-pool64-control/check.log 2>&1
cargo furiosa-opt build --release --bin test_physical_pool --bin compare_physical_pool_group --bin compare_physical_pool_history > experiments/physical-pool64-control/build.log 2>&1

a005.name: a005-physical-pool32-server-resolved
a005.purpose: Rebuild unchanged gated physical32 plain server with resolved Cargo.lock captured before build for reproducible candidate freeze; no CPU rerun
command:
set -e
cargo check --locked --bin server > experiments/physical-pool32/server-resolved-check.log 2>&1
cargo furiosa-opt build --release --bin server > experiments/physical-pool32/server-resolved-build.log 2>&1

assessment: c080 runtime uses rings0..39 and d40, incompatible with sourcephysical32. Shared target library freshness is a supported hypothesis, not yet independently reproduced as the unique cause. The cached7a library mtime is during a00464 build; a00532 logs only bin/greedy compile, and relative src dep-info plus older32 source mtimes can explain stale reuse.
valid_separate_evidence: Frozen32/64 micro/model executables and actual10GiB memory differences remain independent; c080 server/public results are quarantined, not physical32 serving evidence.
mitigation: Preserve first clean build, add actual runtime workspace/Buffer extent validation and startup identity, force all package source mtimes fresh before final build, capture immutable ELF and verify source hashes.
